summary: Exam-proctor evasion tool bundling a browser cookie decryptor and stealth Electron shell
details: Package published under a benign 'Windows Diagnostic Utility' description is an exam/proctor-evasion utility. It ships a PowerShell script (bin/chrome_cookies.ps1) that uses DPAPI + AES-256-GCM to decrypt Chrome/Edge/Brave cookies for.openai.com and.chatgpt.com, and main.js injects the recovered cookies into an Electron session.defaultSession to load https://chatgpt.com in a hidden bridge window. Stealth affordances include WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE on windows, TOOLWINDOW/NOACTIVATE styling, a watchdog that respawns the process, and copying the Electron binary to SearchFilterHost.exe (kalamasha-tool.js). A bundled ~27MB uia_extract.exe and a SendInput-based auto-typer are also present. Cookies are read from the operator's own browser profile and used locally against the operator's own ChatGPT account; no lifecycle hook exfiltrates data to an author-controlled destination, and no attacker-controlled network endpoint is contacted. The child_process/ping and http/GET patterns matched by a static rule are local-process management and internal Electron traffic, not exfiltration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
